title: Conscience
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Conscience is the inward witness that bears moral testimony, accusing or defending a person’s actions. Because conscience can be weak, seared, defiled, or misinformed, it must be instructed by Scripture and cleansed through Christ.
summary: Conscience is the inward witness that bears moral testimony, accusing or defending a person’s actions. Because conscience can be weak, seared, defiled, or misinformed, it must be instructed by Scripture and cleansed through Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ cleanses the conscience from dead works through His blood. In Him, believers are freed from false guilt and called to walk with a conscience shaped by truth and love.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Conscience is a gift of God, but it is not the final authority. It bears witness within a person, accusing or excusing, but it must be shaped by truth because sin can distort moral judgment.

Scripture speaks of a good conscience, weak conscience, defiled conscience, and seared conscience. This means conscience can be overly sensitive, dangerously hardened, or trained wrongly by sin, fear, culture, or false teaching.

The conscience needs the Word of God. Feelings of guilt are not always accurate, and lack of guilt does not always prove innocence. Scripture, not conscience alone, defines righteousness and sin.

Christ cleanses the conscience through His sacrifice. Believers do not have to live under dead works, false guilt, or unresolved condemnation. They are called to walk in truth, love, and sincerity before God.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people are ruled by either a crushed conscience or a hardened conscience. Some feel guilty where Scripture gives freedom, while others feel peace where Scripture warns of sin.

This doctrine helps believers seek a conscience trained by God’s Word and cleansed by Christ’s blood. It protects from both legalistic bondage and careless disobedience.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not treat your conscience as God, but do not ignore it either. Bring conviction, guilt, and moral uncertainty under Scripture. Ask Christ to cleanse your conscience, repent where God’s Word exposes sin, and receive freedom where the Gospel answers false guilt.
